related_questions.question: What is the status of student loan forgiveness?

text_blocks.snippet: The Department of Education has temporarily paused student loan forgiveness under certain income-driven repayment (IDR) plans due to a court order. The pause impacts plans like SAVE, Income-Contingent Repayment (ICR), and Pay As You Earn (PAYE) because a court ruled that the Education Department exceeded its authority in approving these plans. The Department is recalculating payment counts to address the court's concerns and will resume forgiveness once system updates are complete, though no timeline has been provided.

list.snippet: Pause on Certain IDR Plans: The pause affects forgiveness under SAVE, ICR, and PAYE plans.
IBR Plan: While the pause affects other IDR plans, the Income-Based Repayment (IBR) plan is still eligible for forgiveness under certain conditions.
Payment Count Adjustments: The Department of Education needs to recalculate how many payments count toward forgiveness after a court ruling.
Resumption of Forgiveness: Forgiveness will resume once the Department completes necessary system updates.
No Timeline: A specific timeline for resuming forgiveness has not been announced.
Borrowers Should Stay Informed: Borrowers should keep their contact information updated and monitor for updates from their loan servicers and the Department of Education.

text_blocks.snippet: On May 5, 2025, the US Department of Education will resume collecting on defaulted federal student loans for the first time since the COVID-19 pandemic began in March 2020. This means that borrowers in default will face potential consequences like wage garnishment and offset of federal payments such as tax refunds. The Department of Education is also relaunching an enhanced Income-Driven Repayment (IDR) process to simplify enrollment.

text_blocks.snippet: Student loan forgiveness programs are currently facing legal challenges and operational pauses. Specifically, forgiveness under certain income-driven repayment plans, like SAVE, PAYE, and ICR, is paused due to a court ruling questioning the authority for these plans. The pause impacts borrowers enrolled in these plans, including the SAVE plan, which is a key initiative of the Biden administration.

list.title: Legal Challenges:
list.snippet: A court ruling last summer challenged the legality of certain income-driven repayment plans, including SAVE, PAYE, and ICR, asserting that Congress did not authorize these plans.

list.title: Pause on Forgiveness:
list.snippet: As a result, the Department of Education has paused loan forgiveness under these plans.

list.title: Impact on Borrowers:
list.snippet: This pause affects millions of borrowers enrolled in these plans, including those in the SAVE plan, which was designed to be a more generous repayment option with lower monthly payments and faster forgiveness.

list.title: IBR Plan:
list.snippet: While forgiveness under SAVE, PAYE, and ICR is paused, forgiveness under the Income-Based Repayment (IBR) plan, which was enacted by Congress, is also temporarily paused while the Department of Education recalculates payment counts impacted by the court ruling.

list.title: Future of Forgiveness:
list.snippet: The Department of Education is working to address the legal issues and recalculate payment counts to resume forgiveness for IBR borrowers as soon as possible.
